courses.title: Foundations of Hospitality
courses.description: Introduction to lodging, food service, and event management in venues ranging from rural inns to enchanted conference centres. Covers guest reception, ward-enhanced room maintenance, and basic service standards expected across the Sown Expanse.
courses.subject: Hospitality Management

courses.title: Service Operations and Guest Experience
courses.description: Operational systems for hotels, banquet halls, and tourist sites, including staff scheduling, enchanted inventory tracking, and complaint resolution. Students learn to design guest experiences that accommodate diverse populations, including travelling True Sires and their security needs.
courses.subject: Hospitality Management

courses.title: Strategic Hospitality Management
courses.description: Advanced management of hospitality enterprises, covering financial modelling, brand positioning, and regulatory compliance under Breedhaven's commercial ward standards. Includes case studies of resorts, university dining, and diplomatic lodging during state visits.
courses.subject: Hospitality Management

courses.title: Ethics of Everyday Magic
courses.description: Introduction to moral reasoning about common magical practices: household wards, Bloom suppressants, fertility assays, and enchantments embedded in consumer goods. Students examine consent, privacy, and the line between personal magic and public harm.
courses.subject: Magical Ethics

courses.title: Consent and Magical Agency
courses.description: Examines the ethics of magical influence on autonomy, focusing on the Bloom's pull, reproductive contracts, and warding practices that affect others without explicit agreement. Contrasts Bloomist and Freewill frameworks through case law and philosophical argument.
courses.subject: Magical Ethics

courses.title: Advanced Topics in Magical Ethics
courses.description: Seminar on contested ethical frontiers: mandatory dampers in safety-critical professions, disclosure of Sire status, magical enhancement during pregnancy, and the state's interest in reproduction. Students produce a research paper on a self-selected regulatory dispute.
courses.subject: Magical Ethics

courses.title: Introduction to Public Safety
courses.description: Foundations of protective services in a magitech society, including patrol procedure, incident reporting, and basic ward-based security systems. Weekly lab practises situational awareness, radio protocol, and non-magical restraint techniques suitable for campus enforcement.
courses.subject: Public Safety

courses.title: Ward Security and Threat Response
courses.description: Design and operation of layered ward systems for public buildings, events, and protected-person details. Weekly lab covers ward-bridge diagnostics, counter-enchantment field response, and evacuation procedures for magical incidents in crowded spaces.
courses.subject: Public Safety

courses.title: Protective Operations and Sire Security
courses.description: Capstone course in executive and high-value protective operations, emphasising True Sire escort detail, threat assessment, and coordination with national Sire Registry enforcement. Weekly lab runs simulated protection scenarios under graduated magical and physical pressure.
courses.subject: Public Safety

courses.title: The Living Bloom
courses.description: Introduction to the Primordial Bloom as an active presence in soil, water, and blood. Covers the foundational texts, the Seven-to-One ratio, and the theological distinction between the Bloom's generative pull and a woman's sovereign will.
courses.subject: Bloom Theology

courses.title: Bloom and Civilization
courses.description: Examines how the Bloom's influence has shaped law, agriculture, and family structure across the Sown Expanse. Compares Breedhaven's constitutional traditions with neighbouring states' approaches to the Bloom's role in public life.
courses.subject: Bloom Theology

courses.title: Seminar in Bloom Theology
courses.description: Graduate seminar on contemporary theological debates: the nature of the Bloom's want, post-menopausal magic, and the ethics of magical augmentation through pregnancy. Students engage with current scholarship and produce an original paper.
courses.subject: Bloom Theology

courses.title: Kitchen Fundamentals
courses.description: Introduction to professional kitchen practice: knife skills, stock production, and food safety in both conventional and enchanted kitchens. Weekly lab covers basic cookery, yeast cultivation, and the principles of heat transfer in warded ovens.
courses.subject: Culinary Arts and Brewing

courses.title: Brewing and Fermentation Science
courses.description: The biochemistry and magical theory of fermentation, covering beer, cider, mead, and Bloom-infused cordials. Weekly lab practises batch brewing, yeast management, and quality control, with attention to Breedhaven's orchard-based brewing traditions.
courses.subject: Culinary Arts and Brewing

courses.title: Enchanted Cuisine and Menu Design
courses.description: Advanced cookery integrating culinary technique with deliberate magical effect, including Bloom-resonant dishes for seasonal festivals and restorative meals for pregnant women. Weekly lab develops tasting menus that balance flavour, nutrition, and magical coherence.
courses.subject: Culinary Arts and Brewing

courses.title: Principles of Economy
courses.description: Introduction to supply, demand, and market structure in a magitech economy where enchanted infrastructure and reproductive demographics shape production. Covers currency, trade, and the economic role of True Sires within Breedhaven's tax and contract framework.
courses.subject: Economics

courses.title: Labour and Demographic Economics
courses.description: Examines how the Seven-to-One ratio and Sire scarcity affect labour markets, household formation, and public spending. Students analyse damper markets, reproductive contract valuation, and the economics of wards as public goods.
courses.subject: Economics

courses.title: Regulation and the Magitech Economy
courses.description: Advanced seminar on economic regulation in Breedhaven and the wider Sown Expanse: ward standards, Sire Registry policy, agricultural enchantment subsidies, and competition among magitech firms. Students model policy outcomes using current national data.
courses.subject: Economics

courses.title: Foundations of Strength Training
courses.description: Introduction to resistance training, conditioning, and movement mechanics for students of all body types and Bloom states. Weekly lab covers proper lifting technique, programme design, and safe training practices for pregnant and non-pregnant students alike.
courses.subject: Strength and Conditioning

courses.title: Programme Design and Athletic Performance
courses.description: Intermediate strength and conditioning theory, including periodisation, sport-specific training, and recovery protocols that account for the Bloom's physical demands. Weekly lab practises programme assessment, load management, and coaching cues for mixed-ability groups.
courses.subject: Strength and Conditioning

courses.title: Advanced Strength and Conditioning
courses.description: Theory and practice of physical training for peak performance, integrating exercise physiology with Bloom-enhanced recovery techniques. Weekly lab involves supervised programming, load testing, and performance assessment in the Foundry's kinematics bay. Taught by Coach Grushka Tor-Vael.
courses.subject: Strength and Conditioning

courses.title: Foundations of Public Administration
courses.description: Introduction to the structures and functions of government in Breedhaven, from the Crown and Assembly to municipal wards and Bloom-ward offices. Covers the history of civil service, the role of women in governance, and the basic frameworks of public budgeting and regulatory oversight. Taught by Professor Corwenna Ashby.
courses.subject: Public Administration

courses.title: Public Policy and Implementation
courses.description: Examines how policy moves from Assembly debate to enacted regulation, including the role of the civil service, enforcement agencies, and the courts that govern reproductive and paternity law. Students analyse case studies from recent legislation affecting Sire protections, damper regulation, and agricultural subsidy. Taught by Professor Corwenna Ashby.
courses.subject: Public Administration

courses.title: Seminar in Governance and Reform
courses.description: Graduate seminar on contemporary challenges in Breedhaven public administration, including the management of the Sire Registry, cross-border policy in the Sown Expanse, and the capacity constraints of governing a state where seven in eight citizens are women. Taught by Professor Corwenna Ashby.
courses.subject: Public Administration

courses.title: Introduction to Bloomology
courses.description: Foundational study of the Primordial Bloom as a natural force: its presence in soil, water, and blood, its observed effects on living things, and the basic principles by which women channel it. Weekly lab introduces measurement of Bloom fields and basic exercises in directed enchantment. Taught by Dr Maelis Varn.
courses.subject: Bloomology

courses.title: Bloom Dynamics and Field Theory
courses.description: Intermediate study of how the Bloom behaves as a field, including resonance, attenuation, and the well-documented amplification that occurs during pregnancy. Weekly lab involves field mapping, controlled resonance experiments, and safety protocols for working with amplified Bloom states. Taught by Dr Maelis Varn.
courses.subject: Bloomology

courses.title: Applied Bloomology and Enchantment Design
courses.description: Advanced study of the Bloom as an engineering material: how wards and enchantments are structured in everyday objects, and how Bloom principles are integrated into modern infrastructure. Weekly lab involves designing, testing, and calibrating original enchantments in the Foundry. Taught by Dr Maelis Varn.
courses.subject: Bloomology

courses.title: First-Year Expanse Languages
courses.description: Introduction to the major languages of the Sown Expanse beyond Breedhaven, with emphasis on practical communication, reading, and the cultural context of neighbouring states. Students choose a primary language track and may sample a second. Taught by Dr Halcyon Reed.
courses.subject: Foreign Languages

courses.title: Intermediate Language and Translation
courses.description: Continued development of reading, writing, and conversational fluency in the student's chosen language track, with introduction to translation theory and the particular challenges of rendering magical and legal terminology across Expanse cultures. Taught by Dr Halcyon Reed.
courses.subject: Foreign Languages

courses.title: Advanced Language and Cross-Cultural Discourse
courses.description: Advanced study of the student's chosen language, engaging with primary sources in literature, law, and natural philosophy from across the Sown Expanse. Particular attention is paid to how different states describe the Bloom, gender, and inheritance in their own traditions. Taught by Dr Halcyon Reed.
courses.subject: Foreign Languages

courses.title: Foundations of Sire Genetics
courses.description: Introduction to the genetics of the sex ratio and True Sire fertility, covering the Bloom's role in sex determination, the clinical assay that establishes Sire status, and the basic biology of inheritance in the Sown Expanse. Weekly lab involves microscopy, assay demonstration, and basic genetic analysis. Taught by Dr Ottilie Marrow.
courses.subject: Sire Genetics

courses.title: Inheritance and Population Genetics
courses.description: Intermediate study of inheritance patterns in populations with extreme sex ratios, including the mathematics of Sire frequency, genetic drift in small populations, and the legal and social frameworks that manage paternity and lineage. Weekly lab involves population modelling and paternity-case analysis. Taught by Dr Ottilie Marrow.
courses.subject: Sire Genetics

courses.title: Advanced Topics in Sire Biology
courses.description: Advanced seminar on the frontiers of Sire genetics, including unusual assay profiles, the interaction between Sire fertility and Bloom field strength, and the ethics of genetic counselling in a society organised around reproductive scarcity. Weekly lab involves independent research projects. Taught by Dr Ottilie Marrow.
courses.subject: Sire Genetics

courses.title: Government and the Breedhaven State
courses.description: Introduction to the constitutional structure of Breedhaven: the Crown, the elected Assembly, the courts, and the conventions that have shaped government since the founding of House Dawnbloom. Covers the role of the heir's education and the relationship between custom and statute. Taught by Professor Isaura Penhallow.
courses.subject: Government

courses.title: Political Theory and the Bloom
courses.description: Surveys the major political traditions of the Sown Expanse, with particular attention to the Bloomist and Freewill schools and their competing claims about the relationship between the Bloom's influence and legitimate authority. Students read primary sources from both traditions and contemporary critics. Taught by Professor Isaura Penhallow.
courses.subject: Government

courses.title: Comparative Governance in the Sown Expanse
courses.description: Comparative study of the political systems of the Sown Expanse, examining how different states have organised government, law, and reproductive policy around the same biological and magical realities. Case studies include Breedhaven, its neighbours, and states outside the Expanse. Taught by Professor Isaura Penhallow.
courses.subject: Government

courses.title: Agricultural Systems and the Bloom
courses.description: Introduction to modern agriculture in Breedhaven, covering soil science, riverine irrigation, and the role of the Bloom in crop growth and soil health. Weekly lab involves field sampling, soil Bloom measurement, and basic crop assessment at the university's experimental orchards. Taught by Professor Petra Lindqvar.
courses.subject: Agricultural Sciences

courses.title: Crop Science and Enchantment Integration
courses.description: Intermediate study of crop management in a Bloom-saturated environment, including the use of wards against blight, growth enchantments in orchard systems, and the interaction between conventional fertilisation and Bloom-mediated nutrient cycling. Weekly lab involves enchantment trials and yield analysis. Taught by Professor Petra Lindqvar.
courses.subject: Agricultural Sciences

courses.title: Advanced Agriculture and Land Stewardship
courses.description: Advanced study of agricultural management at scale, including river-system governance, orchard economics, and the long-term sustainability of Bloom-intensive farming in Breedhaven's lowland ecology. Weekly lab involves independent research and a field project with a working orchard. Taught by Professor Petra Lindqvar.
courses.subject: Agricultural Sciences

courses.title: Introduction to Magical Engineering
courses.description: Foundations of engineering with the Bloom, covering the principles by which enchantments are structured into materials, circuits, and devices, and the safety standards that govern magical engineering in Breedhaven. Weekly lab in the Foundry introduces basic enchantment construction, measurement, and calibration. Taught by Dr Benedek Hale.
courses.subject: Magical Engineering

courses.title: Enchantment Circuits and Resonance
courses.description: Introduction to the design and fabrication of embedded enchantment systems in everyday devices. Weekly laboratory covers inscription techniques, resonance tuning, and safe handling of charged components. Prerequisite: MEN 101 or permission of instructor.
courses.subject: Magical Engineering

courses.title: Ward Architecture and Power Systems
courses.description: Advanced theory of structural wards, grid-scale enchantment distribution, and the integration of Bloom-derived power with mechanical and electrical systems. Weekly laboratory involves design, testing, and failure analysis of ward networks under load. Prerequisite: MEN 201.
courses.subject: Magical Engineering

courses.title: Foundations of Breedhaven Law
courses.description: Survey of the Breedhaven legal system: constitutional structure under House Dawnbloom, the Assembly, courts, and the hierarchy of statute and custom. Introduces legal reasoning, case analysis, and the basics of civil and criminal procedure.
courses.subject: Law

courses.title: Reproductive and Sire Law
courses.description: The law of paternity, inheritance, reproductive contracts, and the protections surrounding True Sires. Covers the Sire Registry, consent and coercion statutes, and the reproductive courts. Case method throughout.
courses.subject: Law

courses.title: Constitutional Law and the Crown
courses.description: The constitution of Breedhaven, the powers and limits of the monarchy, the prerogatives of the Assembly, and the legal position of the heir. Examines the custom of royal education, succession, and the relationship between custom and statute. Prerequisite: LAW 101.
courses.subject: Law

courses.title: Women, Magic, and Society
courses.description: Introduction to the study of women's lives under the Bloom: magic, generativity, labor, and power. Covers the Bloomist and Freewill traditions, the history of damper use, and the social organization of reproduction.
courses.subject: Women's Studies

courses.title: The Bloom and the Self
courses.description: Examines the lived experience of the Bloom's pull: instinct, identity, and the question of choice. Topics include damper culture, maternal and non-maternal generativity, and feminist critiques of Bloom determinism. Prerequisite: WST 101 or permission of instructor.
courses.subject: Women's Studies

courses.title: Advanced Seminar: Freewill and Bloomism
courses.description: Capstone seminar on the central debate of women's studies: whether the Bloom's wants are a woman's own. Students engage primary philosophical and political texts, produce a substantial research paper, and present to the colloquium. Prerequisite: WST 201 and one additional WST course.
courses.subject: Women's Studies

courses.title: The Bloom in History
courses.description: A general-education survey of the Primordial Bloom as a historical force, from oral traditions and early natural philosophy to its role in the founding of the Sown Expanse's modern states. No prerequisites.
courses.subject: History of the Bloom

courses.title: Psychology of the Bloom
courses.description: Introduction to the psychological dimensions of the Bloom in women: the generative drive, its developmental trajectory, its intensification in pregnancy, and its absence after menopause. Covers damper effects and the psychology of True Sire proximity. No prerequisites.
courses.subject: Bloom Psychology

courses.title: Reproductive Biology of the Sown Expanse
courses.description: The biology of the seven-to-one sex ratio, True Sire fertility, and the mechanisms by which pregnancy amplifies a woman's magic. Weekly laboratory introduces assay techniques, basic histology, and statistical analysis of fertility data. No prerequisites.
courses.subject: Reproductive Biology

courses.title: Prenatal Thaumaturgy
courses.description: Survey of the magical changes of pregnancy and their practical applications and risks. Weekly laboratory covers measurement of gestational thaumic output, prenatal warding, and safety protocols for pregnant practitioners. No prerequisites.
courses.subject: Prenatal Thaumaturgy

courses.title: Household Enchantment and Management
courses.description: Practical and theoretical introduction to the enchanted household: built-in wards, preservation charms, heating and lighting systems, garden magic, and the domestic economy of a magitech home. No prerequisites.
courses.subject: Household Studies

courses.title: Calculus and Statistics
courses.description: Differential and integral calculus with an introduction to probability and statistics, emphasizing applications in magical engineering, thaumic measurement, and biological assay. No prerequisites.
courses.subject: Calculus and Statistics

courses.title: Introduction to Computing
courses.description: Fundamentals of programming, data structures, and algorithms, with applications to enchantment modeling, ward simulation, and Registry database systems. Weekly laboratory covers hands-on coding and debugging. No prerequisites.
courses.subject: Computer Science

courses.title: Rhetoric and Debate
courses.description: Principles of argumentation, persuasion, and public speaking. Students analyze and construct arguments on topics of public controversy, including Bloom policy, Sire regulation, and royal prerogative. No prerequisites.
courses.subject: Rhetoric and Debate

courses.title: Peoples and Politics of the Sown Expanse
courses.description: Comparative survey of the nations and peoples of the Sown Expanse: their governments, economies, magical traditions, and relations with Breedhaven. Covers the regions beyond the Expanse and the status of migrants and outsiders. No prerequisites.
courses.subject: Peoples and Politics of the Sown Expanse

courses.title: Studio Art Foundations
courses.description: Introduction to drawing, painting, and sculptural practice, with attention to the use of Bloom-infused pigments and materials. Weekly laboratory provides guided studio time and critique. No prerequisites.
courses.subject: Studio Art

courses.title: Music Theory and Practice
courses.description: Foundations of melody, harmony, rhythm, and form, with an introduction to resonant and thaumically enhanced instruments. Weekly laboratory includes ensemble performance and ear training. No prerequisites.
courses.subject: Music
